memo.headline: Most of the drop from last month is the usual October dip (NYC fell the same way last year). The money actually being lost is in three fixable places: a broken iOS payment step in Berlin and Amsterdam since 7 Oct (about €28k a week), London Edition 30 selling out after 3 days with 29 days left (about €122k at risk), and Madrid's Autumn special running far behind pace (€120k unsold, 12 days left).

data_sufficiency.explanation: The funnel and sales numbers are large: thousands of iOS checkouts per market, and every key rate change passed compare_rates with p≈0 after correcting for the number of segments scanned. Year-on-year weeks exist for 9 of the 12 markets. How much each channel actually adds is only directional. There is one natural experiment (Milan brand search, 14 days off), and the attribution models disagree a lot. Mexico City is 8 weeks old and small, at about 580 orders in 28 days.

kpis.name: Gross revenue (first-party, 12 markets)
kpis.note: -11.7% vs the previous 28 days. Against the same period last year (9 markets with history) it is -2.5% (€1,856,965 vs €1,904,256). Berlin and Amsterdam alone are -23% YoY (€286,966 vs €372,920). The other 7 markets are +2.5% YoY.

kpis.name: Marketing spend
kpis.note: +3.4%, mostly Barcelona (+€3.1k) and the Mexico City ramp-up (+€3.2k).

kpis.name: MER (revenue / spend)
kpis.note: Overall target is ≥10. Markets missing it: Mexico City 7.12, New York 8.82, Berlin 9.71, Amsterdam 9.96.

kpis.name: Orders
kpis.note: -11.9%. New York (-2,132) and Berlin+Amsterdam (-1,800) account for most of it.

kpis.name: Blended CAC
kpis.note: Target ≤€16. Markets missing it: Mexico City €24.64, New York €17.87, Amsterdam €16.77. Payback is over the 0.6-order target in Mexico City (0.90) and New York (0.64); Amsterdam sits at 0.60.

kpis.name: Platform-claimed vs first-party revenue
kpis.note: Meta claims €703,797 against €521,138 first-party; TikTok claims €171,465 against €100,594. First-party TikTok ROAS is 2.78, under the 3.0 target.

findings.title: iOS payments broke in Berlin and Amsterdam on 2026-10-07 (both markets, same day)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout→order: Berlin 65.9% → 36.1% (1,856/2,815 → 908/2,516); Amsterdam 64.8% → 36.0% (1,423/2,197 → 764/2,125). Both are 'different' after correcting for 36 market×device comparisons. In the last week, add_payment→purchase was 25.3% in Berlin (132/521) and 25.2% in Amsterdam (117/465), against about 70-75% before. Rage clicks on /payment (iOS) per 1,000 sessions: Berlin 6.9 → 347.6, Amsterdam 13.9 → 368.2. Android and desktop are normal, and so is Paris iOS (11.5). Exit survey: 'payment_failed' 19.4% in Berlin and 21.6% in Amsterdam vs about 5.5% elsewhere. Revenue YoY by week went from about 0% to -36% (Berlin) and -35% (Amsterdam). Money: about 726 + 604 orders, €82.5k lost in 28 days; about €28k a week while it stays unfixed. This is also why Berlin (MER 9.71) and Amsterdam (9.96, CAC €16.77) now miss target.

findings.title: London Edition 30 sold out on 3 Oct-15 with 29 days left; its capacity of 267 looks like a setup error
findings.evidence: LON-P029 capacity is 267, against 3,013-3,043 for London Editions 27-29. It sold out on 2026-10-15, three days after launch, at about 66.8 units a day. Exit survey 'sold_out' is 12.1% of 2,441 London answers vs 4.8% elsewhere, 213 of them about Edition 30. About €42k lost so far and €122k more at risk if not restocked. London total revenue still held (+17-18% YoY in the last two weeks).

findings.title: New York's 35% drop is seasonal, not a product-page bug
findings.evidence: NY revenue: €232,967 vs €360,915 last month, but €239,889 in the same weeks last year (-2.9%). Last year's weekly revenue fell the same way (€87.8k → €62.6k at the start of October). The why-not-buy engine's 'iOS product page' cause is the same seasonal pattern: view→cart fell on every device (iOS 31.8% → 22.4%, Android 30.6% → 22.6%, desktop 29.0% → 22.7%), and fell the same way last year (iOS 32.7% → 26.0%). Brand-search impressions fell 32% (15,024 → 10,187), which means less demand. Spend stayed flat at about €6.6k a week, so NY misses MER (8.82 vs 10), CAC (€17.87 vs €16) and payback (0.64 vs 0.6). Spend at stake: €26.4k per 28 days.

findings.title: Madrid Autumn special is far behind pace, and shoppers say the price is the problem
findings.evidence: MAD-P027 has sold 864 of 3,022 (28.6%) with 77.4% of its window gone. It sold 136 units in the last 7 days and has 12 days left, so at this pace about 1,900 units go unsold. Unsold value is €120,006 at €55.61. In the exit survey 'price' is 25.4% of 1,847 Madrid answers vs 16.7% elsewhere, 402 of them about this product. Madrid's other editions are on pace (Edition 30 at 30.9% sold vs 31.0% of window elapsed).

findings.title: Paris Video A (PAR-META-1) is worn out
findings.evidence: Frequency rose from 1.84 to 5.29 over 7 weeks. Weekly CTR fell from 1.39% to 0.64%. Over 28 days CTR fell from 1.36% to 0.88% (7,637/561,183 → 4,952/562,656), 'different' after correcting for 84 ads. First-party ROAS fell from 6.77 to 2.68 last week, under the 3.0 target, while UGC C (PAR-META-3) earned 6.39 at frequency 1.92. Spend at stake: about €1k a week.

findings.title: Mexico City is behind earlier launches, mainly on the product page and on trust
findings.evidence: Revenue/spend over weeks 0-7 since launch: Mexico City 7.16 (€48,664 / €6,799), São Paulo 7.82, Miami 9.16. The market is also about one-third the size. view→cart is 19.4% (1,651/8,531) vs Miami 29.7% (7,953/26,800), 'different'. It has been about 19-20% since launch week, so it is structural, not a recent break. The exit survey shows 'trust' at 21.7% of 414 answers vs 7.8% elsewhere. Last 28 days: MER 7.12, CAC €24.64, payback 0.90 orders, all missing target. MEX-GGL-GENERIC spent €717 for €500 of revenue (CPA €89.58, about 4.5x the €20 target). The engine sizes the product-page gap at €18.8k lost in 28 days.

findings.title: London: Meta's last-click revenue moved to email, while the market total stayed flat
findings.evidence: From the week of 2026-09-28, London email revenue doubled (about €10k → €22-25k a week) and Meta last-click revenue fell (about €21k → €12-15k a week), while total London revenue stayed at €83-86k a week. London Meta and TikTok CPMs rose about 38% the same week (Meta about €7.0 → €9.5-10.2), putting London's CPM at 10.8 vs the 9.0 target. The lower Meta last-click ROAS (4.87 vs 6.6 paid) is therefore not a reason to cut London; it reflects attribution and auction cost.

findings.title: Channel credit is unsettled: brand search and TikTok are the open questions
findings.evidence: Brand search share of credit: 15.2% last click, 33.5% on journey last touch, 20.9% data-driven. First-party ROAS is 17.27 on €19,972. In the Milan natural experiment (brand off for 14 days), market revenue went €107,585 → €101,000 (-6.1%) while organic+direct rose €42,770 → €57,673, absorbing about 81% of the €18,424 brand revenue. That points to partial incrementality, but -6% is inside normal weekly noise (8%). TikTok: platform claims 1.70x first-party; data-driven credit is 7.6% vs 4.4% last click. Generic search: first-party ROAS 2.21 (under the 3.0 target), but data-driven credit is 7.0% vs 2.7% last click, so don't cut it on last-click numbers alone.

findings.title: Barcelona will overspend its October budget
findings.evidence: 93.4% of €20,481 is spent with 80.6% of the month gone. At the 28-day run rate (about €753 a day) it ends the month about €3.2k (≈15%) over. The extra spend is earning: paid ROAS 6.24 and YoY revenue +9% (€258,060 vs €236,178).

recommendations.action: Urgent ticket to engineering: fix iOS payment failure in Berlin and Amsterdam (started 2026-10-07)
recommendations.why: Both markets broke on the same day, on iOS only, at the payment step. Rage clicks on /payment rose about 25-50x and 'payment_failed' leads the exit survey. Something released or changed on 7 Oct (payment provider, Apple Pay, a local payment method or a script) is the likely cause. This is the biggest leak in the business.
recommendations.expected_impact: Get iOS add_payment→purchase back from about 25% to about 70%. That is worth about €28k a week (about 460 orders a week) across the two markets, and brings Berlin and Amsterdam back above MER 10 and CAC €16.
recommendations.how_to_measure: iOS add_payment→purchase rate in Berlin+Amsterdam over the last 7 days. Baseline 0.2525; target ≥0.65.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN step='purchase' THEN users END)/SUM(CASE WHEN step='add_payment' THEN users END),4) AS value FROM events_daily WHERE device='ios' AND market IN ('Berlin','Amsterdam') AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM events_daily), '-7 days')

execution.note: P1 – Berlin and Amsterdam, iOS only: payment step failing since 2026-10-07. iOS checkout→order 65.9%→36.1% (Berlin) and 64.8%→36.0% (Amsterdam); last week add_payment→purchase 25%. /payment rage clicks per 1,000 iOS sessions: 6.9→347.6 (BER), 13.9→368.2 (AMS); Android, desktop and other markets normal. Exit survey 'payment_failed' about 20%. Check releases, payment provider and wallet config, and locale-specific payment methods deployed around 7 Oct. About €28k a week lost.

recommendations.action: Ticket to ops: check and restock London Edition 30 (LON-P029); its capacity of 267 looks like a setup error
recommendations.why: It sold out 3 days after launch with 29 days left. Capacity is 267, against about 3,000 for every other London edition. Shoppers are leaving because it is sold out.
recommendations.expected_impact: If capacity can be raised to the usual level, about 66.8 units a day: up to €122k over the remaining window. If it cannot, the note asks to point London ads and email at Edition 29, which has €80.7k unsold and is slightly behind pace.
recommendations.how_to_measure: LON-P029 units sold in the last 7 days. Baseline 0 (sold out).
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(units),0) AS value FROM product_daily WHERE product_id='LON-P029' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM product_daily), '-7 days')

execution.note: London: LON-P029 (Edition 30) capacity 267 vs 3,013-3,043 for Editions 27-29; sold out 2026-10-15 with 29 days to run (sold about 66.8 a day). 'sold_out' 12.1% of London exit-survey answers. Please confirm whether 267 is a data-entry error and restock to the intended capacity. If capacity cannot be raised, tell growth so London traffic is redirected to Edition 29 (LON-P028, 61.8% sold vs 64.3% of window elapsed).

recommendations.action: Send an email flow for Madrid Autumn special (MAD-P027) to opted-in Madrid customers
recommendations.why: It is 28.6% sold with 77.4% of its window gone and 12 days left, which leaves €120k unsold. Price is the top non-browsing exit reason in Madrid (25.4% vs 16.7% elsewhere), mostly about this product. Email is the cheapest reversible lever and reaches people who already buy.
recommendations.expected_impact: Lift weekly units from 136 to about 250+. Each extra 100 units is about €5.6k. If the owner allows a price incentive in the flow (see questions), expect more.
recommendations.how_to_measure: MAD-P027 units in the last 7 days. Baseline 136.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(units),0) AS value FROM product_daily WHERE product_id='MAD-P027' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM product_daily), '-7 days')

execution.note: Madrid only. Last-chance flow for Autumn special (ends 2026-11-06): 1,900+ places left at €55.61. Lead with value and the end date. Send in two waves, one now and one 5 days before the end.

recommendations.action: Run an A/B test on the Mexico City product page: add trust signals (local reviews, secure-payment and refund guarantee, local payment methods shown on the page)
recommendations.why: Mexico City view→cart is 19.4% vs Miami's 29.7% ('different'). It has been low since launch, and 'trust' is 21.7% of exit answers vs 7.8% elsewhere. Spend nearly tripled (€1.8k → €5.0k), so the leak gets bigger as the market scales.
recommendations.expected_impact: A +25% relative lift (19.4% → 24.3%) would add about 400 add-to-carts per 28 days. The engine sizes the full gap at €18.8k a month, and the change would move MER (7.12) and CAC (€24.64) toward target.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Mexico City view_product→add_to_cart over the last 14 days. Baseline 0.1973.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN step='add_to_cart' THEN users END)/SUM(CASE WHEN step='view_product' THEN users END),4) AS value FROM events_daily WHERE market='Mexico City' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM events_daily), '-14 days')

execution.note: Mexico City only. A = current product page; B = trust block above the fold (local reviews and ratings, secure payment and refund guarantee, local payment methods such as OXXO and cards in MXN, delivery and date clarity). Primary metric view→add_to_cart; 1,116 product viewers per arm (about 1-1.5 weeks at about 2,100 viewers a week).

recommendations.action: Rotate out worn-out Paris Video A (PAR-META-1) and give its budget to the other Paris Meta ads
recommendations.why: Frequency is 5.29, CTR is down 35% ('different' after 84 comparisons) and ROAS was 2.68 last week, under target, while UGC C earns 6.39 in the same market.
recommendations.expected_impact: About €1k a week moves from ROAS about 2.7 to about 5-6 (META-2 and META-3), which is about +€3k revenue a week. Paris Meta ROAS should rise from its 14-day baseline of 4.71.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Paris Meta first-party ROAS over the last 14 days. Baseline 4.71.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(s.revenue)/(SELECT SUM(spend) FROM ad_daily WHERE market='Paris' AND platform='meta' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily), '-14 days')),2) AS value FROM sales_daily s WHERE s.market='Paris' AND s.channel='paid:meta' AND s.day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily), '-14 days')

execution.note: Paris Video A fatigued: frequency 1.84→5.29, weekly CTR 1.39%→0.64%, ROAS 2.68 last week. Budget goes to PAR-META-2 and PAR-META-3. Brief creative for a refreshed Video A (see experiments).

recommendations.action: Trim New York paid spend by 10% through the seasonal low and watch total revenue against last year
recommendations.why: NY demand drops every October (it did last year too). Spend stayed flat, so NY misses MER, CAC and payback targets. Platform-claimed returns overstate what paid adds, and we have no proof that the last 10% of NY spend is incremental. A small cut that is easy to reverse tests that cheaply.
recommendations.expected_impact: Saves about €2.6k per 28 days. If NY's YoY revenue gap (currently -3% to -10% a week) does not widen, the spend was not adding sales; if it widens by more than the saved spend x 3, restore it.
recommendations.how_to_measure: New York MER over the last 14 days (baseline 8.16), read against NY weekly YoY in v_market_yoy.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT ROUND((SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM sales_daily WHERE market='New York' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily), '-14 days')) / (SELECT SUM(spend) FROM ad_daily WHERE market='New York' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily), '-14 days')),2) AS value

execution.note: Seasonal trim: NY revenue -35% vs September, the same as last year (-2.9% YoY for the period), spend flat at about €6.6k a week. MER 8.82 vs target 10, CAC €17.87 vs €16. Reverse if the YoY revenue gap widens by more than 3x the saved spend.

recommendations.action: Pause Mexico City generic search (MEX-GGL-GENERIC)
recommendations.why: €717 spent for €500 first-party revenue. CPA is €89.58 vs the €20 target and ROAS 0.70; even the platform claims only 0.78. Generic search gets more credit in the data-driven model in mature markets, but even 2.6x that credit would leave it under 3.0 here.
recommendations.expected_impact: Saves about €720 per 28 days with little revenue risk, and raises Mexico City MER (14-day baseline 7.44).
recommendations.how_to_measure: Mexico City MER over the last 14 days. Baseline 7.44.

execution.note: Mexico City generic search: 28d spend €716.65, 8 orders, CPA €89.58 (target €20), ROAS 0.70 (target 3.0). Revisit once the product-page test improves conversion.

recommendations.action: Ask the growth manager to decide on Barcelona's October overspend: allow about €3.2k over budget or cap it
recommendations.why: Barcelona is 93.4% spent at 80.6% of the month gone. The extra spend is earning (paid ROAS 6.24, revenue +9% YoY), so this is a budget-policy call, not a performance problem.
recommendations.expected_impact: Avoids a surprise overspend of about €3.2k, or knowingly keeps about 6 days of profitable spend.

Madrid's regular Edition 29 is on pace (63.1% sold vs 64.3% elapsed).

findings.title: Brand search looks mostly non-incremental, but this is not yet proven
findings.evidence: Brand search takes 14.9% of last-click revenue, 34.2% of journey last-touch and 21.2% data-driven, at €19.8k of spend in 28 days with ROAS 10.5–21. In the Milan natural experiment (MIL-GGL-BRAND off 2026-08-16 to 08-29), market revenue went from €109,227 to €106,853 (−2.2%). Organic and direct rose from €42,740 to €62,294 and absorbed most of the campaign's €20,651. The 14 days afterwards came in at €104,296, so the small dip may just be trend. That is one market over 14 days.

findings.title: Mexico City is behind earlier launches, mainly on its product page and trust
findings.evidence: Weeks 0–7 cumulative revenue/spend: Mexico City 7.07 (€47,839 / €6,771), São Paulo 7.91, Miami 9.26. Product view to add-to-cart is 19.3% (1,619/8,375) vs 29.7% in other markets, significant after 12 market comparisons. 'trust' is 21.7% of exit answers (80 vs 24 the prior period). Paid ROAS is 2.18 vs the target of 3. MEX-GGL-GENERIC spent €727 for 4 orders (CPA €181.76, ROAS 0.41). Even at the 2.4x data-driven uplift generic search gets overall, that would only bring back about €711. Market MER is 6.97 vs 10 and CAC €28.18 vs €16.

findings.title: Barcelona is overspending its budget with no extra revenue to show for it
findings.evidence: Weekly spend rose from about €4.5k to about €5.2k from the week of 09-28. Weekly revenue stayed at €56.8k–63.5k, about where it was before. Paid ROAS fell from 6.41 to 5.82. The budget is 94.0% spent with 80.6% of the month gone. At €747/day, October would end around €23.1k against a €19.8k budget.

findings.title: London paid social got about 40% more expensive per impression from 28 September; email revenue doubled at the same time
findings.evidence: LON-META-1 CPM went from €6.88–7.06 to €9.58–9.94 with CTR unchanged (about 1.4%). London Meta impressions fell 29% on flat spend, and the market CPM of €10.64 misses the €9 target. London paid revenue fell from €164.4k to €129.6k. Email rose from about €10k to €21–23k a week from the same week, and total London revenue held flat (€344.8k vs €345.6k, +11% YoY). The cause is not in the data. It could be an auction change, a CRM change, or attribution moving between channels.

findings.title: Platforms claim more revenue than first-party sales show, TikTok most of all
findings.evidence: TikTok claims €164,945 vs €97,374 first-party (1.69x). Meta claims €724,909 vs €536,518 (1.35x), Google €439,865 vs €406,850 (1.08x). On first-party numbers, TikTok misses the €20 CPA target on LON-TT-2 (€30.89), AMS-TT-2 (€30.01) and BER-TT-1/2 (€26.4). All 12 generic search ads miss it (€20.43–181.76). The data-driven model does credit TikTok (7.4%) and generic search (7.0%) with more than last click does (4.3% and 2.9%).

Better to settle the question with a test than keep paying on an assumption. Berlin has its own payment outage, so judge its result against Berlin's own pre-break weeks or start the test after the fix.
recommendations.expected_impact: Pauses about €2,464 a week (€14.8k over 6 weeks). If Milan's result holds, nearly all of that is saved for a revenue loss under 5%. The test detects changes of 5% or more.

questions_for_owner: Was anything released on the payment page or payment provider for Germany and the Netherlands around 7 October (Apple Pay, 3DS, script update)?
Was London Edition 30 deliberately limited to 276 units, or is that a set-up error? Can it be restocked?

Did the London email programme change from 28 September (cadence, list or discounts)? Email revenue doubled while paid social revenue fell, so it may be taking credit from paid rather than adding sales.
Can Madrid Autumn special's price or bundle be changed in its last 12 days, or is email the only lever?
New York usually recovers in early November. Do you want New York spend held flat through the dip, as last year, or trimmed for 2 weeks? I recommend holding it.
Should Barcelona's October overspend (about €2.4–3.3k) be absorbed or offset from November's budget? Finance should know either way.
